summary: A rule-clean one-line cap on a host int derived from num_tokens. It is backed by the landed decode_layer cap-16 gain and by this problem's next-larger regression. It adds the one new point neither in-flight sibling covers (bs=256 at 16), and each moving shape is its own scored load, so one run reads per shape with no companions.
justification: I checked the picks against master's kernel_fn. The rule is num_tokens*8/32/bsm < 0.9, and the loop exhausts at 64. That gives bs=1/4/8/16 -> 8, bs=32/33 -> 16, bs=128 -> 48 (32/48 = 0.67) and bs=256/257 -> 64 (64/64 = 1.0 is not < 0.9, so the loop exhausts). After min(.,16), bs=128 goes 48->16 and bs=256/257 go 64->16, and every bs<=33 is unchanged, as the hypothesis states. Profile of the parity best (fb2cc736613747df): Marlin is 495 us (96%) of bs=128 against a 101.3 us floor, and 612 us (96%) of bs=256 against 108.9 us, so both run at about 5-6x SoL. That is the per-m-block compute/latency regime where thread_m_blocks dominates, not an HBM-bound one. Evidence for the direction: (1) next-larger here took bs=128 from 48 to 64 and Marlin went 495 -> 662 us, a 14% shape loss; at bs=32 16->32 lost 21%; (2) decode_layer marlin-block-m-cap-16 (0730135cdcac43b7) made this same min() change and gained 1.10-1.15x at T=128 and 1.08-1.13x at T=256. Each of bs=128 and bs=256 is 1/6 of the geomean, so a 10%+ Marlin change is well above the ~1.5-2.5% drift. Expected directions match: bs=128/256 faster, bs<=32 flat as in-run controls. Weakest link: bs=256 under this problem's skewed busiest-GPU routing. About 2048 routes spread over 8 GPUs gives roughly 256-400 local routes over 32 experts, so the mean is about 8-12 per expert, but the hot experts may hold 30-60. With block 16, each hot expert pays 2-4 m-blocks, each another pass over its w13/w2 slice. decode_layer's T=256 gain came under different routing (dist=soft, 256-expert align), so its magnitude at bs=256 transfers only loosely. bs=128 is on firmer ground because two reasons point the same way: the m-block counts there are smaller, and the next-larger gradient was measured on this problem.
confounders: sglang-marlin-path-parity (landed; align over the bank's 32 experts instead of 256): sorted_ids capacity is M*8 + 32*(bsm-1), so a smaller block slightly shrinks the align padding work (<~1 us against 500-600 us of Marlin). That cannot flip a sign. It does mean decode_layer's 256-expert-align magnitude transfers only approximately. Reverting it would restore the 0.006x dense starter, so there is no meaningful counterfactual and no ab-revert.
interference: No companions. The only diff is one host-side int, and the shapes it moves (bs=128, bs=256) are separate scored loads, each paired with SGLang in the same run. bs=1/8/16/32 keep their pick and act as in-run drift controls. A gain or a loss at either shape reads directly as 'cap 16 beats / loses to SGLang's pick at that shape', so neither sign is ambiguous. The sweep the hypothesis wants is already covered by the in-flight siblings from the same master: next-smaller gives bs=128 at 32 and bs=256 at 48, and verify-two-smaller gives bs=128 at 16 and bs=256 at 32. This run adds bs=256 at 16, which completes 48/32/16 at bs=256. Its bs=128 row repeats verify-two-smaller's exact pick (16), so it costs nothing extra and serves as a reproducibility read for that sibling. An ab-tune of the cap (e.g. 32) would duplicate verify-two-smaller at bs=256, and a control isolating w13 vs w2 cannot change the adopt/reject decision for a single shared block size. One base caveat: if a sibling lands first and master's pick code changes (e.g. to an idx-step table), claim on the new master and put the min() after whatever the final pick is. On top of verify-two-smaller, this run would then move only bs=256 (32 -> 16), which is still readable.
open_questions: At bs=256, compare against verify-two-smaller (32) and next-smaller (48). If 16 loses to 32 there while bs=128 at 16 gains, read it as hot-expert m-block re-streaming under skew. In that case land a per-shape pick (16 at bs<=128, 32 at bs>=256) rather than a uniform cap.

bs=257 and the skewed bs=128 correctness tests run block 16. Marlin supports moe_block_size 16 at any M, and the math and fp32 reduce are unchanged, so correctness risk is minimal. Still, confirm that the run's test list passes before reading timing.

Since this run and verify-two-smaller share the bs=128 pick exactly, if both harvest as gains at bs=128 the promotion should take only one of them. They edit the same line, so a by-hand pick is needed: prefer whichever bs=256 point wins.
If bs=128 gains here, a natural follow-up is whether the w13 and w2 Marlin calls want different block sizes (w2 has size_m = M*8 rows of K=size_n). That is out of scope for this run.
